msg: DATASHEET (AD8226, REFERENCE TERMINAL, printed p.20: 'source impedance to the REF terminal should be kept below 2 ohm'). Closed-loop output impedance of the U2A buffer at DC with the calibrated ro = 1 kohm: measured 0.43 milliohm, i.e. the requirement is met by four orders of magnitude. This is the bench that replaces the inference - TI states OPA2333's open-loop output impedance ONLY at f = 350 kHz (2 kohm typ) and gives no DC or closed-loop figure at all.
DATASHEET, same rule, taken as a maximum across the whole DC..60 Hz band in which the AD8226's 106 dB CMRR minimum is specified (Table 3, CMRR DC to 60 Hz). Measured 0.17 ohm.
DATASHEET, same rule, evaluated on the pessimistic ro = 2 kohm bracket (TI's own literal 350 kHz number). Measured 0.85 milliohm.
DATASHEET, same rule and band, pessimistic bracket. Measured 0.34 ohm.

FINDING, not a pass/fail promise: at 1 kHz - the top of the signal band - the 2 ohm rule is NO LONGER met. Closed-loop Zout rises as ro*f/GBW, giving 2.86 ohm here (calibrated ro). Warning rather than error because the datasheet's 2 ohm sits in its DC/60 Hz CMRR context, this board's common mode is a static 1.65 V (REQUIREMENTS Q1) with no 1 kHz common-mode signal to reject, and the resulting CM gain error Rref/100k = 2.9e-5 corresponds to 90.8 dB - at or above the AD8226's own 90 dB minimum at 5 kHz. See OPEN in the report.
Same finding on the pessimistic ro = 2 kohm bracket: 5.71 ohm at 1 kHz, about 84.9 dB of CM gain error.
FINDING. Frequency at which the buffer's Zout crosses the datasheet's 2 ohm: 700 Hz with the calibrated ro. The bound keeps it clear of the 60 Hz band the CMRR minimum is specified over.
Same crossing on the pessimistic bracket: 350 Hz.
